nodes.summary: The frequency of allele `A` in state `i` is `bernstein.z i = i / M` (for `M = 0` it is Lean's junk value `i / 0 = 0`).
nodes.title: Allele frequency of a Wright–Fisher state

nodes.summary: The heterozygosity `H(j) = 2 (j/M) (1 - j/M)` of state `j`: the probability that two gene copies drawn with replacement carry different alleles.
nodes.title: Heterozygosity of a Wright–Fisher state

nodes.summary: Almost-sure absorption: a Wright–Fisher chain is almost surely eventually absorbed in `0` or `M` (Ewens 2004, ch. 3).
nodes.title: Almost-sure absorption of the Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: The finite Wright–Fisher chain under the canonical Markov law almost surely reaches an endpoint. The law and chain are not premises supplied by a caller.
nodes.title: Finite Wright–Fisher chain is absorbed almost surely

nodes.summary: Path-level fixation probability (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): a Wright–Fisher chain started from `i` copies ever reaches `M` (fixation of `A`) with probability `i / M`.
nodes.title: Fixation probability of a Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: Path-level loss probability: a Wright–Fisher chain started from `i` copies ever reaches `0` (loss of `A`) with probability `1 - i / M`.
nodes.title: Loss probability of a Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: Under the canonical finite Wright–Fisher law, the probability of ever losing the allele at `0` equals `1 - i / M`.
nodes.title: Loss probability of an allele in the finite Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: Under the canonical finite Wright–Fisher law, the probability of ever fixing at `M` equals the initial allele frequency `i / M`.
nodes.title: Fixation probability of the finite Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: Heterozygosity decays geometrically (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): `∑ j, P^t(i, j) H(j) = (1 - 1/M)^t H(i)`. For `M = 0` both sides are `0` because `H ≡ 0` (the factor `1 - 1/0 = 1` is then irrelevant).
nodes.title: Geometric decay of heterozygosity under Wright–Fisher drift

nodes.summary: Martingale property of the allele count (`t` steps): `∑ j, P^t(i, j) j = i`.
nodes.title: Multi-step martingale property of the Wright–Fisher allele count

nodes.summary: Heterozygosity decays by the factor `1 - 1/M` per generation (one step). For `M = 0` both sides are `0` because `H ≡ 0`.
nodes.title: One-step decay of heterozygosity under Wright–Fisher drift

nodes.summary: Martingale property of the allele count (one step): `∑ j, P(i, j) j = i`.
nodes.title: One-step martingale property of the Wright–Fisher allele count

nodes.summary: The probability of sitting in an interior state `0 < j < M` at time `t` tends to `0`.
nodes.title: Interior Wright–Fisher states vanish in the limit

nodes.summary: Fixation probability (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): started from `i` copies, allele `A` is fixed with limiting probability `i / M`, i.e. `P^t(i, M) → i / M`.
nodes.title: Fixation probability in the Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: Loss probability: started from `i` copies, allele `A` is lost with limiting probability `1 - i / M`, i.e. `P^t(i, 0) → 1 - i / M`.
nodes.title: Limiting loss probability of the Wright–Fisher transition matrix

nodes.summary: Path-level fixation probability: if `X` is a Wright–Fisher chain (in the sense of `IsFiniteMarkovChain`) started from `i` copies, then `P(X_t = M) → i / M`.
nodes.title: Limiting fixation probability of a Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: The rows of the Wright–Fisher matrix are Mathlib's binomial laws `Bin(M, i/M)`.
nodes.title: Wright–Fisher rows are binomial laws

nodes.summary: The state `M` (allele `A` fixed) is absorbing.
nodes.title: Fixation of an allele is absorbing in the Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: The state `0` (allele `A` lost) is absorbing.
nodes.title: Loss of an allele is absorbing in the Wright–Fisher chain

nodes.summary: Entries of the Wright–Fisher matrix.
nodes.title: Entries of the Wright–Fisher matrix

nodes.summary: The neutral Wright–Fisher transition matrix on `M` gene copies (Ewens 2004, ch. 3): `P(i, j) = (M choose j) (i/M)^j (1 - i/M)^(M - j)`, the binomial law `Bin(M, i/M)` of the number of `A` copies among `M` draws with replacement. The model needs `M ≥ 1`; for `M = 0` (where `i / M` is Lean's junk value `0`) the matrix is the one-state chain, which is `Bin(0, p) = δ₀` for every `p`.
nodes.title: Neutral Wright–Fisher transition matrix

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
